names.name: chicken riggies
names.said: Riggies is rigatoni. Ask for hot and you get cherry peppers; ask for sweet and you get the other kind.

text.what: An Italian-American pasta dish from the Utica–Rome area of New York: chicken, rigatoni, and hot or sweet peppers in a spicy cream-and-tomato sauce. Variations are many; the peppers and the rigatoni are the constants.
text.story:
Its origin is unclear, and many chefs from the Utica area claim the dish.

*Inference —* that sentence is the same sentence upstate New York keeps writing about its own food. A hundred miles west, three Bellissimo accounts and one John Young compete over a wing; here a dozen Utica kitchens compete over a pasta, and in neither case does a document settle it. What both traditions do instead is hold contests.
text.how: Brown chicken, build a sauce of tomato and cream, and load it with peppers — cherry peppers for heat, sweet peppers for the other way. Toss through rigatoni, whose ridges and bore hold a sauce that thin-walled pasta would shed.
text.today: Served across the Utica–Rome corridor as a restaurant staple and a home dish. *Tradition holds —* riggies, greens and half-moons are the three things a Utica table names as its own.
